comment: The validate chain's cost, as data. FACTORY-SIDE ONLY — this file lives in scripts/ and
NO consumer gate reads it. That placement is the whole design: perf-baseline.json's own
header justifies its ratchet by saying 'Bytes are hardware-independent, so this check is
deterministic everywhere, agent time included'. Milliseconds are not. Shipping a
wall-clock ceiling into template/base/tools/ would put a machine-dependent verdict in a
consumer's turn, on hardware the harness has never seen.
These are the harness's own GitHub-hosted runner's numbers and they are NOT portable.
It replaces two inline shell literals in .github/workflows/selftest.yml ('-gt 120' with a
'-gt 90' warning). Those were not data, not versioned, not per-step, and not visible to
scripts/check-claims.mjs — so a chain that got slower produced an unattributed wall-clock
failure naming no step.
ceilingMs is a CHOSEN policy value and may ship. measuredMs is a MEASUREMENT and may not
be invented: it stays null until a real selftest run records one in a reviewed commit.
Until then check-claims.mjs refuses any wall-clock figure in README.md, which is why that
file still carries none. Measure, commit the measurement, then publish — in that order.
0.6.0 BUILT THE WRITER THE PARAGRAPH ABOVE ASSUMED. Until then nothing could record a
measurement at all: check-chain-budget.mjs judged the numbers against ceilings and threw
them away, so step one of that ordering had no implementation and measuredMs has been null
since this file was introduced. It is now `node scripts/check-chain-budget.mjs <log>
--record`, which stamps a `measurement` block alongside — recordedOn, the RUNNER it came
from, and the chain step COUNT. The runner string is required rather than inferred, because
a number with no provenance is worse than null: it licenses a published figure no CI run can
reproduce. The step count is what stops a figure measured against a 31-step chain from going
on licensing prose after the chain reached 33 — hasCommittedMeasurement compares it to the
live chain, which is arithmetic over two committed values and therefore clockless.
And the ordering is enforced now, not merely prescribed: check-claims.mjs imports
hasCommittedMeasurement and reds on any wall-clock figure in README.md or the latest
CHANGELOG entry while this file carries none. That sentence was here before the control was.
THE FIRST MEASUREMENT LANDED 2026-08-09, from selftest run 31307386944 (the post-0.7.0
reviewed dispatch). The validate half is the CI artifact verbatim. The stop half was
re-derived from the same run's log AFTER review rejected the artifact's: the first-match
timings parser had stamped stopWall from the nested validate member's line — 33 validate
step names, zero stop rows matched — and the stop judge passed it vacuously. Both defects
are pinned in tests/gates/chain-budget.test.mjs; recording from a downloaded CI log with
an explicit --runner is the blessed path check-chain-budget.mjs's own header describes.

defaults.comment: A step with no row below is judged against its class ceiling. Class is decided by whether the step shells out to a toolchain (pnpm exec / tsc / next) or is pure node over the tree.

stopComment: 0.7.0 (W7): the STOP chain's cost, same doctrine as everything above. Nine rows — the
floor∪config Stop union minus `validate`, whose cost IS the `wall` row above (a
stopSteps row naming it is itself a red, so the same number is never judged twice).
The subject is the VALIDATE_TIMINGS line a `node tools/validate.mjs --stop-chain
--report-all` run emits — the emitter is shared — captured by the bootstrap-linux
selftest job with the Supabase stack live and stamps warm (the turn-end latency an
agent actually waits through, not the fail-closed CI shape) and judged by
`node scripts/check-chain-budget.mjs <log> --stop-chain`. The row closure covers the
union, so a future injected Stop step forces a budget row exactly like a validate
step does today; a stale row reds the same way.
Ceilings are CHOSEN policy, per step, with NO class defaults: nine members whose
natures differ too much for two classes to be honest. The two coverage-instrumented
unit suites dominate turn latency — jest-expo's RN transform pipeline is the
documented slow tail, vitest next — and rls-isolation pays live database round-trips
(db reset + pgTAP + the SDK cross-tenant suite). The five static scans get tight
ceilings on purpose: a static Stop step that needs more than a handful of seconds has
stopped being the cheap half of its control, and 'a Stop gate that takes a minute is
a Stop gate people disable'. stopWall is the whole chain wall-to-wall INCLUDING the
nested validate member, ceiling 10 min with the warn band at 75% like the wall above.
Every measuredMs SHIPPED NULL until 2026-08-09 for the same reason wall.measuredMs did:
a measurement may not be invented. `--record --stop-chain` (workflow_dispatch only, same
reviewed-dispatch path as the validate recording step) stamps them from a real run — the
committed numbers are run 31307386944's, re-derived post-review (see the header's last
paragraph for why the artifact's own stop half did not survive it).

rls-isolation.comment: live Supabase round-trips: db reset + the pgTAP structure suite + the supabase-js cross-tenant suite

unit.comment: coverage-instrumented vitest across the workspace — the first of the two dominant suites

mobile-unit.comment: jest-expo with coverage — the RN transform pipeline is the chain's documented slow tail; the largest single ceiling in this file

diff-coverage.comment: reads the two merged istanbul maps the unit steps just wrote plus a git diff — no toolchain

duplication.comment: token-clone scan over apps/*/src + packages/*/src — pure node but O(source tokens), so it gets the widest static ceiling

i18n.comment: static source scan: hardcoded user-facing strings and out-of-seam Intl/toLocale*/toFixed

test-quality.comment: static test scan (~50ms today: assertion presence, .only, dead .skip) — room to grow, never to shell out

mobile-perf.comment: closure half only — reads three files (routes, Maestro flows, startup budget); the measurement half lives in the CI perf lane

reviewer-verdicts.comment: reads reviewer triggers + the turn ledger tail — the turn-scoped step, never a toolchain
